correctness.rationale: For n≥2, |S|≥2 and S≠{0,n}, each admitted cube vertex is a vertex and P_{n,S} full-dimensional. The Löwner/D-optimal covariance duality follows by perturbing a maximizing design: (x−m)^T C^{-1}(x−m)≤n for all x; the average enclosure+AM–GM proves globally smallest determinant including off-center competitors. Symmetrization over coordinate permutations loses no determinant and reduces to rank moments µ=E J, ν=E J² inside polygon conv{(j,j²)}. Covariance eigenvalues V/n and T/[n(n−1)], where V=ν−µ²,T=nµ−ν, so ellipsoid squared axes are V and T/(n−1). The only positive-domain stationary point is cube moment q=(n/2,n(n+1)/4), giving ball centered at 1/2. Otherwise optimizer lies on upper extreme chord or lower consecutive-rank chords of moment polygon, never at pure-rank vertex (zero V). On chord a<b, unique p maximizes p(1−p)[A+p(B−A)]^{n−1}, stationarity A+[n(B−A)−2A]p−(n+1)(B−A)p²=0. The leverage L(j) is quadratic in j; equality at a,b and any third would force cube moments, so exactly those two ranks contact in anisotropic case. Independent exact SymPy n=8,S={0,1,5}: p=(25+√1129)/72 satisfies stationarity, origin leverage (617+19√1129)/168≈7.47<8. All rank subsets, not only consecutive slices; finite numerical check is not proof.
